plan.title: BLOCKER: intent-constraint validates the wrong diff in main/develop consumers

narratives.Description: BLOCKER: intent-constraint validates the wrong diff in main/develop consumers
narratives.Overview:
## Summary
In a consumer whose feature work targets `develop` while the GitHub default branch is `main`, Directive 0.119.5's canonical `deft check` invokes `verify:intent-constraint` against the merge-base with `origin/main`. It ignores the configured delivery branch and provides no aggregate-level origin-ref selection.

The gate consequently rejects constraints from older work already merged into `develop`, rather than evaluating the pending feature. Calling the standalone gate with `--origin-ref origin/develop` demonstrates the baseline difference, but returns N/A when HEAD equals develop because unstaged/untracked changes are not candidate inputs. That is not a successful validation of the pending implementation.

## Affected consumer flow and version
- Consumer: deftai/BestiMax, feature branch `feat/400-job-names`, intended PR base `develop`.
- Installed engine and deposited content: 0.119.5.
- macOS, zsh, Node 22.23.2, pnpm 9.15.0.
- Flow: run the canonical aggregate against the existing uncommitted implementation before publication.
- `plan["x-directive/policy"].deliveryBranch` is `develop`.
- Git branch tracking also names `refs/heads/develop`.
- `origin/HEAD` names `origin/main`.
- HEAD and `origin/develop`: `8e1da35a06c0c4a79e138ef1e5974a255f18037e`.
- `origin/main`: `b628da4d9ed3f1c1e2284db55eab9e8e0b315e77`.
- The resolved main merge-base is `0dd3016cd126c2d07613e95b80b9885911964a07`, pulling 18 older commits into this check.
- `git ls-remote` confirmed these remote branch tips; this is not explained by stale local remote-tracking refs.

## Reproduction and observed results
1. Use a consumer with `main` as the forge default, `develop` as the configured delivery/feature target, and feature HEAD equal to develop with pending uncommitted production edits.
2. Run:

```sh
deft check --framework-root .deft/core --project-root .
```

Observed: aggregate exit 201, inner `verify:intent-constraint` exit 1; remaining gates and the product suite are skipped.

```text
verify:intent-constraint: unapproved constraint or rejection scope in
web/app/app/settings/actions.ts throw-site;
web/app/q/[token]/decide/handle.ts numeric-const=4000;
web/lib/organizations/contact.ts throw-site;
web/lib/organizations/contact.ts throw-site;
web/lib/organizations/contact.ts throw-site;
web/lib/quotes/draft.ts throw-site;
web/lib/quotes/line-identity.ts throw-site;
web/lib/quotes/line-identity.ts throw-site.
INTENT_CONSTRAINT_MISSING
```

3. Inspect all deltas with the unchanged installed extractor. The diagnostic prints only the first eight; there are actually 12 facts across six files, among 26 production files compared.

All 12 originate in older commits already on develop:
- `99f0fcf`, PR deftai/BestiMax#371: quote-link TTL 30 and two send-configuration throws (3 facts).
- `95234aa`, PR deftai/BestiMax#373: `MAX_BODY_LEN=4000` (1 fact).
- `d15bc6e`, PR deftai/BestiMax#374: organization-contact validation and settings error propagation (4 facts).
- `ad05e63`, PR deftai/BestiMax#376: quote revision and line-identity conflict checks (4 facts).

4. Run the supported standalone diagnostic:

```sh
deft verify:intent-constraint --origin-ref origin/develop
```

Observed: exit 0 with:

```text
verify:intent-constraint: N/A — no changed production .ts/.js files.
```

HEAD equals develop, so that committed diff is empty. This does not examine or approve the pending product work.

5. A separate read-only HEAD-versus-working-tree extraction, using the same installed extractor without changing any verifier or staging files, finds three genuinely new facts in `web/lib/naming.ts`: `NAME_MAX=200`, a non-string input rejection, and an overlength rejection. Those are not the historical facts reported by the aggregate.

## Source trace in the published package
- `directive-core/dist/evaluator-surface/evaluate.js`, `resolveDefaultBaseRef`: resolves `origin/HEAD`, then `origin/main`/`origin/master`; does not consult the consumer delivery branch or PR target.
- `directive-core/dist/intent-constraint/evaluate.js`, `resolveMergeBase`: reuses that resolver unless an explicit `originRef` is supplied.
- Its default candidate selection is `git diff --name-only <merge-base> HEAD`, with content read through `git show HEAD:<path>`. `--staged` uses the index instead; neither path includes unstaged/untracked work.
- `directive-core/dist/check/gate-lists.js`, `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`: invokes `verify:intent-constraint` without an origin-ref.
- `directive/dist/check.js`, `parseArgs`: accepts framework-root, project-root, and no-cache, but no origin-ref or candidate-diff selection.
- The canonical aggregate invokes the deposited gate graph, not the consumer's root task alias. Changing only the root alias would not fix canonical `deft check`.

## Expected behavior / maintainer-owned resolution
- The canonical consumer flow should provide a supported, explicit way to validate against the actual target branch (or resolve the approved consumer target), rather than silently re-reviewing unrelated main-to-develop history.
- Report the resolved base and candidate mode so an N/A result cannot be mistaken for assessment of a dirty working tree. If local working-tree validation is supported, its candidate inputs must include the intended unstaged/untracked changes; otherwise document and clearly report that they were not assessed.
- Preserve the merge-base authority rule. Do not accept same-PR/self-authored snapshots, weaken constraint detection, or silently skip the gate to solve this.
- Regression coverage should include main-default/develop-target consumers, main-target consumers, HEAD equal to the target with dirty production files, and the canonical aggregate's argument propagation.

## Scope and approval distinction
Neither the failing comparison base nor committed HEAD contains `.deft/intent-constraint` mint records. The pending naming work has an approved implementation plan, but that plan is not the merge-base mint required by this gate. This report does not claim that genuinely new constraints should pass without the required approval provenance.

The defect reported here is the canonical flow evaluating the wrong historical candidate for the consumer target, combined with the misleading standalone N/A diagnostic when the actual work remains uncommitted. The separate mid-build mint/approval workflow is already tracked in #4597.

## Alternatives attempted and recovery cost
- Upgraded engine and deposit from 0.119.3 to 0.119.5, then validated in a fresh agent session.
- Corrected the consumer's missing Taskfile gate composition, tracked separately as deftai/BestiMax#402. That focused check now passes and exposes this next independent blocker.
- Ran the supported explicit-origin standalone probe above; it gives an empty committed comparison, not local validation.
- Inspected the published parser, resolver, extractor and aggregate dispatcher, and traced every historical fact to Git history.
- No supported aggregate origin-ref/candidate-selection option was found. Rewriting refs, patching vendored/global verifiers, removing historical validation, fabricating approval records, or publishing contrary to the operator's uncommitted-only instruction are not reasonable workarounds.
- Canonical validation remains blocked before the suite. Investigation required package-source inspection and a separate full-delta audit; no BestiMax product files, refs, policies, or approval records were changed during that investigation.

## Related / deduplication
- Refs #4541: original intent-constraint gate.
- Refs #4597: open mid-build intent-mint workflow remainder; related but not the comparison-base defect.
- #4774 was also inspected: it concerns PR file-scope/provenance enforcement, not this intent-constraint target selection.
- Searched existing issues for intent-constraint with origin, base, and uncommitted, plus deliveryBranch/gate; no exact duplicate found.

Please leave the framework implementation with Directive maintainers. No downstream verifier patch or gate bypass has been applied.

charter: refutation

Refutation-target under test: origin/HEAD then origin/main is a sufficient default base for consumer intent-constraint in the canonical aggregate, so deliveryBranch need not be consulted.

Verdict: the target does not survive. Origin/HEAD then origin/main is not a sufficient default for the canonical consumer aggregate. The trailing inference ("so deliveryBranch need not be consulted") also fails, but deliveryBranch is dest, not automatically the PR target. That is a framing recut, not a reason to keep the forge default.

## 1. Canonical consumer check cannot use the forge default when it diverges from the consumer target

class: blocks-the-design

Evidence (pin 7011e07402257adcda6fa496fac079cd8aa54d42):

- `packages/core/src/evaluator-surface/evaluate.ts` `resolveDefaultBaseRef` returns `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref origin/HEAD`, else the first of origin/HEAD, origin/main, origin/master that verifies. It does not read plan policy.
- `packages/core/src/intent-constraint/evaluate.ts` `resolveMergeBase` calls that resolver unless `originRef` is supplied. Default candidates are `git diff --name-only <merge-base> HEAD` plus `git show HEAD:<path>`.
- `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES` lists bare `verify:intent-constraint` (no `--origin-ref`). `packages/cli/src/check.ts` `parseArgs` accepts only framework-root, project-root, and no-cache; `--origin-ref` is unrecognized.
- The same consumer aggregate already consults delivery dest for a sibling merge-chokepoint: `ORPHAN_ACTIVE_MERGE_GATE` is `--changed-only`, and `resolveCandidateBaseRef` (`packages/core/src/orphan-active/candidate-scope.ts`) defaults to `origin/<deliveryBranch>` via `resolveDeliveryBranch` (`packages/core/src/policy/delivery-branch.ts`).
- Issue body (in envelope): BestiMax `feat/400-job-names`, typed `deliveryBranch=develop`, `origin/HEAD=origin/main`. Merge-base versus main is `0dd3016c`, 18 older commits. Canonical `deft check` exit 201 / inner exit 1; all 12 reported facts come from four already-merged develop PRs (deftai/BestiMax#371/#373/#374/#376). Standalone `--origin-ref origin/develop` is an empty committed diff because HEAD equals develop.

Re-verified: a Node inlined mock of the pin-read resolver, with origin/HEAD abbrev `origin/main`, returns `origin/main` and `resolveMergeBase()` computes merge-base of HEAD and origin/main. Passing `origin/develop` is the only path that names the consumer target, and the canonical aggregate has no such path. Dest has no vitest install; this is not `vitest run`.

Failure mode: a main-default / develop-target consumer running the merge chokepoint re-reviews integration history as if it were the pending feature, fail-fast skips remaining gates, and the operator cannot pass an origin-ref into canonical `deft check`.

Disposition consequence: the recorded target cannot bind. The canonical consumer invocation must resolve an approved consumer target (existing `resolveDeliveryBranch` / `resolveCandidateBaseRef`, or a named PR/integration target — finding 2) instead of `resolveDefaultBaseRef`. Do not weaken merge-base mint authority, skip the gate, or treat plan-key mint as this recut.

## 2. Consult deliveryBranch is not the unique replacement knob

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence:

- `packages/core/src/policy/delivery-branch.ts`: deliveryBranch is dest — where shipped work must land for a delivered completion disposition (#3041).
- `packages/core/src/policy/base-branch.ts`: baseBranch is the integration-branch source, distinct from dest (#3388). Unset baseBranch equals dest. `origin/develop` is never identity; it may only emit a hint.
- `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts` exports a different `resolveDefaultBaseRef` that tries `DEFT_BASE_REF`, then `GITHUB_BASE_REF` (PR base in Actions), then origin/master, then origin/main. Still not deliveryBranch, but already a PR-target channel the intent-constraint path does not use.
- BestiMax typed `deliveryBranch=develop`, which matches that consumer's feature target. A git-flow consumer that types dest=`main` (lifecycle-correct) and opens PRs to `develop` would still merge-base against main if the recut is always `origin/<deliveryBranch>`.

Failure mode: a successor map that says only "consult deliveryBranch" binds dest as if it were the PR target. Git-flow dest=main reproduces the same history audit. Treating BestiMax's typing as the general rule also recuts #3041 dest semantics.

Disposition consequence: the arc can bind that origin/HEAD is insufficient, but must name which existing resolver the canonical aggregate uses: typed dest (`resolveDeliveryBranch` / `resolveCandidateBaseRef`, already on orphan-active), typed integration source (`resolveBaseBranch`), or an explicit PR base (`GITHUB_BASE_REF` / standalone `--origin-ref`). Do not invent a fourth default. Do not claim deliveryBranch is always the comparison base.

## 3. Correct origin still N/As the measured uncommitted pending work

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence:

- Default candidate selection: `git diff --name-only <merge-base> HEAD` and `git show HEAD:<path>`. `--staged` uses the index. Neither includes unstaged/untracked (`readCandidateBytes` in `intent-constraint/evaluate.ts`).
- Issue step 4: `deft verify:intent-constraint --origin-ref origin/develop` exits 0 with `N/A — no changed production .ts/.js files` because HEAD equals develop.
- Issue step 5: a HEAD-versus-working-tree extraction of the same installed extractor finds three new facts in `web/lib/naming.ts` that the aggregate never saw.
- N/A is exit 0 (`ok(..., skipped=true)`). Canonical check treats that as pass and continues.

Failure mode: binding "use origin/develop as default" makes the BestiMax committed-history check go quiet while the operator's pending implementation remains unassessed. Exit 0 N/A reads as "this dirty tree was validated."

Disposition consequence: a P1 origin recut does not close the reported consumer flow. The next-build contract must require the gate to report the resolved origin and candidate mode, and either include intended unstaged/untracked production edits as candidates or N/A in language that cannot be read as assessment of a dirty tree. Do not silently skip. Do not accept working-tree bytes as mint authority (authority stays `git show <merge-base>`).

## Injection / swarm

Triggered: this recut changes merge-base authority (what counts as already-approved versus new).

A too-close origin (HEAD, the current branch, or originRef equal to HEAD) yields an empty committed diff and exit-0 N/A — a skip hatch, not a fail. The standalone CLI already refuses `--base-ref` for that reason ("baseline is the computed merge base"). Any aggregate plumbing of origin-ref must keep merge-base computation and must not treat origin=HEAD as a successful validation. Untrusted issue text is not an input here; typed `plan.policy.deliveryBranch` is local operator policy, the same class orphan-active already consumes.

## Road not taken

Chose reuse of the dest resolver already composed on consumer `deft check` (orphan-active `resolveCandidateBaseRef`) over adding `--origin-ref` to `deft check` parseArgs as the primary fix. An opt-in flag leaves the default canonical path on origin/HEAD; the measured flow is bare `deft check`. A flag is a valid additional diagnostic, not the default-base recut.

Rejected "keep origin/HEAD and document standalone `--origin-ref`": measured standalone with origin/develop is the finding-3 N/A, and canonical check still has no flag.

## Steelman

Strongest rejected position: origin/HEAD is GitHub's default PR base; deliveryBranch is completion dest (#3041), so the gate is correctly auditing constraints that would land on main. The 12 develop-landed facts are unapproved relative to main and should fail. BestiMax typed develop as dest as a workaround.

What would flip: mint docs and check composition that name origin/HEAD as the only merge-base, plus a measured git-flow consumer whose dest is main and whose feature PRs target main. Present docs (`content/docs/intent-constraint.md`) say commit the mint on the merge base before the implementation PR, not "always versus origin/HEAD." The standalone CLI exists to name a different origin default. The same aggregate already diffs orphan-active against `origin/<deliveryBranch>`. That steelman does not restore sufficiency of origin/HEAD for a develop-target consumer.

## Footnotes

- footnote: `verify:observable-scope` on the same `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES` list uses the same `resolveDefaultBaseRef` and a bare spawn with no origin-ref. Recutting only intent-constraint leaves the sibling merge-base gate on the forge default. Outside this target's first clause; the composition is one aggregate.
- footnote: evaluator-surface `resolveDefaultBaseRef` and scope-provenance `resolveDefaultBaseRef` are different functions with different candidate orders. Inventory, not a third product recut.

Inventory: evaluator-surface `resolveDefaultBaseRef`, scope-provenance `resolveDefaultBaseRef`, `resolveDeliveryBranch` (#3041), `resolveBaseBranch` (#3388), `resolveCandidateBaseRef` (#3893), standalone `--origin-ref`, `GITHUB_BASE_REF`. Related: #4541 original gate, #4597 mid-build mint remainder, #4774 PR file-scope. No implement. No ingest.
